message.content:
Below is an overview of key tenant rights and protections under Texas law (as of 2024). For specific situations—especially if you’re dealing with a landlord dispute—it’s wise to consult a lawyer or your local housing agency. | Area | What the law says | Practical take‑away | |------|-------------------|---------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlords may charge up to one month’s rent for a furnished unit, two months’ for an unfurnished unit.
• Must be returned within 30 days after lease ends, minus deductions for damages beyond normal wear & tear. | Keep a copy of the lease, document the unit’s condition at move‑in/out, and request a written itemized list of any deductions. | | **Habitability / Repairs** | • Landlord must keep premises safe, sanitary, and fit for habitation (Texas Property Code §92.001‑92.006).
• Tenants can withhold rent only if the landlord fails to make necessary repairs after reasonable notice. | Report problems promptly in writing; give the landlord a “reasonable” time to fix (usually 7–14 days). | | **Notice Requirements** | • For non‑renewal or termination of month‑to‑month leases: 30 days’ written notice.
• For termination of fixed‑term leases before expiration: 30 days’ notice (unless otherwise specified). | Always deliver notices in person, by mail, or via email (if the lease allows electronic communication). | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must file a complaint in district court and serve the tenant with a summons.
• Tenant has 5 days to respond after service.
• Court will schedule a hearing; if the landlord wins, the tenant has 48 hours to vacate. | If you receive a notice, read it carefully, and consider contacting a tenant advocacy group or attorney right away. | | **Rent Increases** | • No statutory limit on how much a landlord can raise rent, but they must give proper notice (usually 30 days for month‑to‑month). | Keep track of all rent increase notices; verify they comply with the lease terms. | | **Discrimination** | • Under federal Fair Housing Act and Texas Civil Rights Code, landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or other protected classes. | If you suspect discrimination, file a complaint with the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) or the Texas Attorney General’s Office. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord must respect your right to privacy and peaceful enjoyment of the property. | If a landlord enters without proper notice (typically 24 hrs), you can refuse entry. | | **Lease Termination** | • Either party can terminate a lease by giving proper notice per the lease agreement.
• Landlord may terminate for cause (e.g., nonpayment, violation of lease). | Review your lease for any special clauses (e.g., early termination fees). | | **Legal Assistance** | • Texas offers free or low‑cost legal aid through community organizations, law schools, and the Texas Legal Services Center. | Contact local tenants’ unions or legal clinics for help drafting notices or representing you in court. | ### Quick Resources | Resource | Link | |----------|------| | Texas Attorney General – Consumer Protection Division | https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov/consumer-protection | | HUD – Fair Housing | https://www.hud.gov/program_offices/fair_housing_equal_opp | | Texas Legal Services Center | https://texaslegalservices.org/ | | Local Housing Authority (search by city) | https://www.hud.gov/topics/housing_assistance | --- #### How to proceed if you have a specific issue 1. **Document everything** – photos, emails, text messages, receipts, and a written log of incidents. 2. **Check your lease** – see what it says about maintenance, notice periods, and rent increases. 3. **Contact your landlord** – put requests in writing and keep copies. 4. **Seek help** – if the landlord doesn’t comply, reach out to a local tenants’ union or legal aid clinic. Feel free to let me know if you’d like a sample notice letter, a template for documenting repairs, or guidance on filing a complaint.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What are my rights as a tenant in the state of Texas?" They want information about tenant rights. We can provide general info. But we might also offer to generate a contract. However the question is not asking for a contract. So no function call needed. Just answer. Provide overview: security deposit limits, notice requirements, habitability, eviction process, etc. Also mention resources like Texas Attorney General's website, local housing agencies. Provide citations. No need to use function.
